A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the REM sleep behavior disorder (RDB) is a disorder of REM sleep characterized by the absence of muscle atonia and the presence of complex and often violent motor activity during REM sleep.
RBD is associated with epileptic seizure.
RBD may be associated with epilepsy and may even be a prodromal symptom of seizures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of RBD should be considered as part of the differential diagnosis of late-onset seizures in elderly men.
the presence of RBD should alert the physician to the possibility of an epileptic seizure disorder, especially in the elderly.
REM behavior disorder is not always benign and that it can be the manifestation of underlying pathology.
